title: Never overwrite a host-edited verify-app projection in onboard
action: Per D11 (issue 100). `pub fn compute_verify_skill_items(` in onboard/plan.rs pushes `copy_verify_skill` for any installed projection where `verify_skill_drifted(&source_walk, &target_walk)` is true, so `onboard --apply` replaces host edits. Record what bee wrote: when apply runs copy_verify_skill (onboard/apply.rs `apply_copy_verify_skill`, which already walks per-file hashes), store the rendered per-file hashes under `.bee/onboarding.json` `managed.verify_skills.<target-rel>` = {<file-rel>: <hash>} (keep it through the payload rewrite that builds `managed`). In the planner, for a drifted projection: a projection file whose hash differs from both the new rendered source and the recorded hash is a host edit — push `verify_blocked_item(name, &rel, "installed", kind, reason)` with reason `installed <rel> has edits bee did not write (<file>) - skipped, never overwritten. FIX: copy the edits into .bee/verify/<name>, then re-run bee onboard --apply` instead of copying. When no record exists yet (first run after this change) fall back to: block only when the differing projection file's mtime is newer than its source file's mtime by more than 2 seconds. `blocked_verify_skill` must not count in `core_changes_needed` (plan.rs), so a blocked projection never keeps onboard at changes_needed or fails install.sh; keep it visible in the plan output. Red first in onboard/tests.rs next to the copy_verify_skill tests (rg -n copy_verify_skill onboard/tests.rs): apply, then edit a projection file, change the source, plan → blocked_verify_skill and apply leaves the edit; an untouched projection with a changed source is still copied; core_changes_needed is false for a plan holding only a blocked_verify_skill item. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.
